definition: Converting written text into spoken audio, covering front-end text normalization through neural acoustic models and vocoders.
details: Converting written text into spoken audio, covering front-end text normalization through neural acoustic models and vocoders. Modern systems produce near-human prosody and support voice cloning.

explainer.lead: The full pipeline that turns written text into spoken audio, from cleaning up the text through neural acoustic modeling to waveform generation. It matters because modern systems reach near-human prosody and can clone voices.

tiers.eli5: It's the whole factory line that takes a sentence you typed and produces a voice saying it, sounding close to a real person.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers split the work into front-end text normalization, neural acoustic models, and vocoders. Pitfall: errors in the front end, such as misreading numbers or abbreviations, propagate into the audio no matter how good the acoustic model is.
tiers.paperLevel: Covers front-end text normalization, neural acoustic models, and vocoders. Known limits from the record: near-human prosody and voice cloning are supported by modern systems; no formal formula is given.

explainer.example: A system normalizes "Dr. Smith paid $5" into spoken-word form, an acoustic model predicts the speech, and a vocoder renders the audio waveform.
